messages:
ari: quick heads-up — noticed a reproducible tail-latency spike on /generate this morning after the kernel-selection change. looks like token-level p95/p99 jump when KV cache warmups overlap with batching fallback :thinking:

sam: ugh. numbers? any SM occupancy or vrm traces?

ari: pasted the short summary from the profiler: p50 12ms -> p95 110ms, p99 230ms. SM occupancy drops from ~86% to ~51% during the spike window. VRAM usage increases by ~600MB at the same time. GPU power + thermal show small bump but nothing alarming.

lee: do you have the batching distribution during the event? small batches can force a different kernel path.

ari: yes — batch histogram attached in the dashboard (link). most requests stayed at batch=1 or 2 — the new batching heuristic tries to prioritize latency and ends up promoting more singletons during high concurrency. that triggers fallback to the generic matmul kernel for small dims.

sam: that explains kernel selection. fallback kernel has worse SM utilization for our attention matmul shapes. can we force fused attention kernel for batch >=2?

lee: we already have a flag BATCH_POLICY=latency_first. When concurrency spikes, the scheduler over-optimizes for immediate dispatch and disables coalescing for 20ms. change we made to avoid queueing hurt us.

maria: also saw high KV cache miss churn. prefix cache miss rate climbed to 23% during the same window. lots of ephemeral sessions cause eviction churn and extra memcpy work. KV cache thrash + small batches = more memory operations and kernel overhead.

ari: pinned snippet from the perf dump:

```
# top hotspots (symbols):
0x7f1a... fused_attention_kernel       48.2%
0x7f2b... generic_matmul_kernel       31.4%  <-- much higher than baseline
0x7f3c... kv_cache_lookup             11.6%  (memcpy + misses)
0x7f4d... scheduler_dispatch          6.8%
```

lee: interesting that generic_matmul is higher — that indicates we are hitting the slow codepath more. if we bias kernel selector to prefer fused for shapes where it exists, we should recover SM occupancy.

ops-bot: perf-alert: token_tail_latency.p99 > 200ms for route:/generate (172 occurrences) — alert muted after ack by ari.

sam: propose quick fix: revert the micro-change to the immediate-dispatch gating and re-enable a 10ms coalescing window. also add an explicit rule: kernel_selector.prefer_fused_for(batch_size>=2 && seq_len<=1024).

ari: agreed. will push hotfix to staging. also adding a temporary KV prefetch throttle to reduce eviction pressure (limit prefetch concurrency to 8).

devex-bot: created PR #4287: "hotfix: restore coalescing window + kernel selector bias" — CI queued.

maria: on the dashboard side, I added a per-route widget: token-latency breakdown (tokenize -> model_infer -> kv_lookup -> postproc) and a GPU panel with SM occupancy, allocated_vram, power_w, temp_c, and MIG slice distribution. link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/eng-runtime/perf-kv-mig?from=now-2h&to=now

lee: after the revert in staging, can we run the synthetic workload that simulates ephemeral sessions? I want to validate KV miss rate goes down and SM occupancy recovers.

ari: running it now. preliminary: p95 back to ~18ms, p99 ~45ms, SM occupancy ~80% stable. KV miss rate dropped to 5%.

sam: awesome. let's run A/B for 24h on canary with both configs and capture per-route KPIs: cost/token, tokens/second, tail latency. also capture MIG slice skew — last time one tenant landed on heavy slice and caused thermal throttling in neighboring slice.

maria: noted. I'll add alert rules: if SM occupancy drops >20% vs baseline for >30s and kv_miss_rate>10% trigger incident and auto-fallback to previous kernel policy.

ari: thanks all. follow-ups: (1) PR to kernel selector and coalescing revert, (2) KV prefetch throttle in runtime, (3) add per-route dashboard panel + automated regression alert.

sam: and add a tiny unit test for kernel selection to make sure small-batch shapes still choose fused when available.

lee: will do.

maria: I'll export the dashboard panels as JSON and attach to the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
